 -3-  MFA No. 103973 of 2016  C/W MFA No. 103770 of 2016  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S.173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 16.07.2016 PASSED IN MVC NO.441/2014 ON THE FILE OF THE PRIL.
SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC AND MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL NO.V, JAMKHANDI, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION.

THESE APPEALS ARE COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this matter is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. Challenging judgment and award dated 16.07.2016 passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge, &
JMFC., and MACT-V, Jamkhandi in MVC no.441/2014, these appeals are filed.
3.

Brief facts as stated are that on 12.01.2014 when claimant Basappa @ Basavaraj Balappagol was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-28/H-2703 on Jamkhandi - Mudhol Road, driver of car bearing registration no. KA- 25/MD-66 drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motorcycle causing accident.
Claimant sustained grievous injuries and despite taking treatment, sustained physical disability.

4. Alleging loss of earning capacity, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'M.V. Act' for short) against owner and insurer of offending vehicle.
5. On service of summons, owner and insurer filed objections opposing claim petition on all counts.
It was specifically contended by insurer that driver of car was not having valid and effective driving licence and there was violation of policy conditions.
6. Thereafter, tribunal framed issues, recorded evidence of claimant as PW.1 and Dr. G.N. Sanadhi as PW.2.
Exhibits P1 to P10 were marked.

Respondents examined RWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exhibits R1 and 2.
7.
On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver and claimant was entitled for compensation.

Though, insurance policy issued with respect to said vehicle was valid on date of accident, on ground that driver was having valid driving licence Basappa @ Basavaraj vs Shivappa @ Shivanand on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4709859/
3 to drive transport vehicle and not light motor vehicle, liability of insurer was discharged and owner was held liable to pay compensation awarded in lumpsum at Rs.1,00,000/-.
8. Aggrieved by said award, claimant has preferred MFA no.103973/2016; while owner has filed MFA no.103770/2016.

9. Sri Mahantesh R. Patil, learned counsel appearing for Sri. S.S. Patil, learned counsel for owner-appellant submitted that there was no dispute about driver of car holding HGV licence valid upto 28.06.2018.
As per Section 7 of M.V. Act, only a person having held driving licence to drive light motor vehicle for a period of atleast one year would be eligible to apply for transport vehicle licence.
It was further submitted that lack of driving licence or knowledge about driving was not either alleged to be reason for causing accident or established.
Therefore presumption has to be drawn about valid and effective driving licence and liability fastened upon insurer.
10. Sri. Siddappa S. Sajjan, learned counsel for claimant- appellant at out set, seconded submission on behalf of owner on liability.
It was submitted that tribunal erred in awarding inadequate compensation.

Insofar as quantum of compensation, it was submitted that claimant aged 38 years,
working as mason was earning Rs.9,000/- per month.

And even though he sustained Grade-II compound fracture of fibula and cut of gastrocnemius muscle etc. which were assessed by PW.2 - Dr.Sanadi to have caused 16% permanent disability to left lower limb, tribunal erred in awarding global compensation, instead of assessing separate compensation towards conventional and non-conventional heads in injury case.
11. On other hand, Sri. N.R. Kuppelur, learned counsel for insurer opposed appeals and supported award.
It was submitted that Ex.R.2 produced by insurer would not indicate that driver of car was holding LMV driving licence.
Therefore, finding of tribunal on liability was justified.
It was further submitted that on over all consideration, award of global compensation with 9% interest per annum would be justified and no interference was called.

12. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
13.
From above submission, it is seen that owner is in appeal on finding regarding liability; whereas claimant is in appeal for enhancement.

Thus points that arise for consideration are:
"1) Whether tribunal was justified in holding owner liable to pay compensation?
2) Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement as sought for?"
14.

Insofar as liability, as rightly contended by learned counsel for appellant, Section 7 of M.V.Act,
does mandate that only a person who has held driving licence to drive light motor vehicle for atleast one year would be eligible for driving licence in respect of transport vehicle.
Admittedly, as per Ex.R.2, driver was having driving licence to drive transport vehicle (HGV) valid as on date of accident.

Moreover, it is not case of insurer that driver did not know driving or that accident Basappa @ Basavaraj vs Shivappa @ Shivanand on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4709859/
4 occurred solely on account of lack of licence, it cannot be held that there was violation of policy conditions.
Therefore, point no.1 is answered in affirmative.

15. Insofar as income, though claimant stated that he was working as mason and earning Rs.9,000/-
p.m. same is not established.
In absence of specific evidence, it has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2014 is Rs.7,500/- as per norms adopted by Karnataka State Legal Services Committee for settlement of cases before Lok Adalath.
Therefore, it has to be taken at Rs.7,500/-.
16. Insofar as disability, claimant produced wound certificate, treatment records and disability certificate.
He also examined Dr.Sanadi as PW.2, who examined claimant and assessed disability to left lower limb at 16%.
Considering occupation of claimant, it would be appropriate to consider loss of earning capacity at 5%.

Applying multiplier of '15', future loss of income would be:
Rs.7,500/- x 5% x 12 x 15 = Rs.67,500/-.
17.

In personal injury claims, tribunal is required to award separate compensation towards pain and suffering, medical expenses, food, attendants and other incidental expenses, future loss of income and loss of income during laid up period, loss of amenities etc.

Considering Grade-II compound fracture of fibula sustained by claimant and disability assessed by P.W.2, it would be appropriate to award Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering; and Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Claimant produced medical bills for a sum of Rs.36,658/-, which is awarded.
18. Normally, fractures take three months to heal.
Therefore, loss of income during laid up period would be Rs.7,500/- X 3 =Rs.22,500/-.
19. Claimant is also awarded Rs.15,000/- towards food, attendants, conveyance and other incidental charges.
Thus, claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,91,658/- as against Rs.1,00,000/- awarded by tribunal.
Point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative.

Hence, following:
ORDER i. MFA No.103770/2016 is allowed.
Insurer is liable to pay compensation.
ii. Amount in deposit is ordered to be refunded to appellant-owner.
iii. MFA No.103973/2016 filed by claimant is allowed in part.
iv. Claimant is held entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.1,91,658/- as against Rs.1,00,000/- awarded by tribunal.
Claimant would be entitled to interest at 6% per annum on enhanced compensation.
